content:
Quick Answer

The median home price in Dunedin is $450,000 as of Q1 2026, up 3.8% year-over-year. Homes spend an average of 32 days on market before going under contract.

Data reflects single-family, townhome, and condo sales in the Dunedin market through March 2026. For a personalized pricing analysis, contact Barrett Henry or call (813) 733-7907.

Dunedin is one of Pinellas County's most charming and walkable communities -- a small-town Gulf Coast city with a Scottish heritage, a thriving downtown, craft breweries on every block, and direct access to Honeymoon Island and Caladesi Island state parks. The housing market here reflects that desirability, with steady price growth driven by limited inventory and strong demand from both local buyers and relocating professionals.

Below is a data-driven breakdown of what is happening in the Dunedin housing market right now, what it means for buyers and sellers, and where prices are headed through the rest of 2026.

Market Snapshot: Dunedin Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025

MetricQ1 2026Q1 2025
Median Sale Price$450,000$433,500
Days on Market3226
Active Inventory142108
Homes Sold (Q1)118126
Price Per Sq Ft$285$274
List-to-Sale Ratio97.1%97.8%
New Listings (Q1)168140
Pending Sales95105

What Is Driving the Dunedin Housing Market?

  • Walkable downtown driving lifestyle demand. Dunedin's Main Street corridor is one of the best walkable downtowns in Tampa Bay, packed with locally owned restaurants, craft breweries, galleries, and shops. Buyers are paying a premium for the ability to walk to dinner, and that premium has only grown as remote work allows more people to prioritize lifestyle over commute.
  • Honeymoon Island and Caladesi Island proximity. Direct access to two of Florida's top-rated state park beaches gives Dunedin an outdoor lifestyle edge that few Pinellas communities can match. The Pinellas Trail runs directly through downtown, connecting to the broader county trail network for biking and running.
  • Limited buildable land constraining supply. Dunedin is a built-out city with minimal vacant land for new development. This structural supply constraint keeps inventory tight and supports price appreciation even as the broader market normalizes. Most new inventory comes from existing homeowner turnover, not new construction.

Home Prices by Property Type in Dunedin

Property TypeMedian Price (Q1 2026)
Single-Family Home$485,000
Townhome$375,000
Condo$295,000

Prices vary significantly by proximity to downtown and waterfront access. Request a custom market report for the specific property type and area you are targeting.

What Do Current Conditions Mean for Buyers?

Dunedin remains competitive, especially for single-family homes within walking distance of downtown. Inventory has increased compared to 2025, giving buyers slightly more options and negotiating room. However, well-priced homes in prime locations still move quickly. Buyers should come pre-approved, and the best strategy is to focus on properties that have been on market 14+ days where sellers may be more flexible. Condos and townhomes offer a more affordable entry point into the Dunedin market.

What Do Current Conditions Mean for Sellers?

Dunedin sellers benefit from strong brand recognition -- the city's reputation as a desirable, walkable community drives consistent buyer interest. The key to maximizing your sale price is presentation. Buyers in this market are often lifestyle-driven and respond to move-in-ready homes with updated kitchens and outdoor living spaces. Price at recent comparable sales, invest in staging and professional photography, and highlight walkability and proximity to downtown amenities. Expect solid offers within 3-4 weeks for well-priced properties.

Dunedin Housing Market Forecast: Rest of 2026

Dunedin home prices are projected to appreciate 3-5% through the remainder of 2026. The combination of limited supply, strong lifestyle demand, and the city's growing reputation as a destination community supports continued growth. The main headwind is affordability -- as prices push past $450K median, some buyers redirect to more affordable Pinellas communities like Palm Harbor or Largo. However, Dunedin's unique walkable character provides a durable price premium that most competing communities cannot replicate.

Frequently Asked Questions About the Dunedin Housing Market

Is Dunedin FL a good place to live?

Dunedin is consistently rated one of the best small cities in Florida. The walkable downtown, craft brewery scene, proximity to Honeymoon Island and Caladesi Island, and strong community identity make it popular with families, professionals, and retirees. The trade-off is higher prices compared to other Pinellas County communities.

What is the average home price in Dunedin FL?

The median home price in Dunedin is $450,000 as of Q1 2026. Single-family homes average $485,000, townhomes around $375,000, and condos around $295,000. Prices vary significantly by location -- waterfront and downtown-adjacent properties command substantial premiums.

Is Dunedin FL expensive?

Dunedin is above the Pinellas County median but below waterfront communities like Clearwater Beach or Belleair. The cost of living is driven primarily by housing costs. Day-to-day expenses like groceries, dining, and utilities are comparable to the broader Tampa Bay average. No state income tax helps offset housing costs.

How far is Dunedin from Tampa and Clearwater?

Dunedin is approximately 5 miles north of Clearwater and 25 miles northwest of downtown Tampa. The drive to Clearwater takes about 10-15 minutes. The commute to Tampa is 35-50 minutes depending on traffic and which bridge you use (Courtney Campbell or Howard Frankland).

What are the best neighborhoods in Dunedin?

Downtown Dunedin and the surrounding historic neighborhoods are the most sought-after for walkability. The neighborhoods along Edgewater Drive offer waterfront living. Areas near Dunedin Golf Club and north Dunedin provide a quieter, more residential feel with larger lots. Each neighborhood has a distinct character and price range.

Is Seminole FL a good place to live?

Seminole is one of the most well-regarded communities in Pinellas County. It offers a suburban lifestyle with good schools, low crime, established neighborhoods, and central access to beaches and Tampa Bay. It is particularly popular with families and retirees seeking a quiet, convenient location.

How far is Seminole from the beach?

Indian Rocks Beach and Indian Shores are approximately 10-15 minutes from most Seminole neighborhoods. Clearwater Beach is about 20 minutes north, and St. Pete Beach is about 25 minutes south. Beach access is one of Seminole's strongest selling points.

What are schools like in Seminole FL?

Seminole feeds into well-regarded schools within the Pinellas County School District. Seminole High School, Seminole Middle School, and several elementary schools in the area maintain solid ratings. The area also has access to Pinellas County's magnet and choice programs.

Is Seminole expensive?

Seminole is mid-range for Pinellas County. At a 0K median, it is more affordable than beachfront communities like Clearwater Beach or Belleair, but above budget-friendly areas like Largo or Pinellas Park. For the combination of schools, location, and lifestyle, most buyers consider it good value.

What is the difference between Seminole and Largo?

Seminole is generally more suburban and residential with higher home prices and school ratings. Largo is larger, more diverse, and more affordable with a wider range of housing options. Both are centrally located in Pinellas County with good beach access. Seminole tends to attract families seeking top schools, while Largo appeals to buyers prioritizing affordability.

  • Diverse housing stock creating multiple market tiers. Clearwater offers everything from 0K mainland condos to M+ beachfront properties. The mainland market serves working families and retirees, while the beach and island markets cater to vacation home buyers and luxury seekers.

What Do Current Conditions Mean for Buyers?

Clearwater buyers have more options than in recent years, especially on the mainland side. Single-family homes on the mainland offer the best value relative to location. Be prepared for bidding competition on well-priced homes near the Countryside or northeast Clearwater areas.

What Do Current Conditions Mean for Sellers?

Clearwater sellers are in a good position, particularly those with homes near the beach or in desirable mainland neighborhoods. The key is pricing realistically for today's market rather than yesterday's peak. Beachside condos with manageable HOA fees sell fastest. Mainland single-family homes with updated kitchens and bathrooms command premiums. Address any deferred maintenance before listing -- buyers are more selective than in 2021.

Clearwater Housing Market Forecast: Rest of 2026

Clearwater home prices are projected to appreciate 3-5% through 2026. The beach proximity premium ensures a floor under prices, while rising insurance and HOA costs could dampen appreciation in the condo segment. Single-family homes on the mainland should see the steadiest growth. Any significant drop in mortgage rates would benefit Clearwater disproportionately, as it would release pent-up demand from rate-sensitive buyers.

Is Clearwater FL a good place to buy a home?

Clearwater offers excellent quality of life with beach access, diverse neighborhoods, and solid property values. The mainland areas provide more affordable options with beach proximity, while Clearwater Beach and Island Estates cater to luxury buyers. Consider insurance costs and condo HOA fees when budgeting.

What is the average home price in Clearwater?

Is Clearwater Beach expensive to live in?

Clearwater Beach is significantly more expensive than mainland Clearwater. Beachfront condos start around 0K and single-family homes on the beach side can exceed M. HOA fees and insurance costs are also higher for coastal properties. Mainland Clearwater offers much more affordable options with a 10-15 minute drive to the beach.

How are the schools in Clearwater?

Clearwater has a mix of school ratings. Northeast Clearwater and Countryside areas tend to have higher-rated schools. Clearwater is part of the Pinellas County School District, which offers magnet and choice programs that allow students to attend specialized schools throughout the county.

Is Clearwater a good place to retire?

Clearwater is one of the most popular retirement destinations in Florida. The combination of beach proximity, healthcare facilities (Morton Plant Hospital, BayCare network), mild winters, and active adult communities makes it ideal for retirees. Many areas offer 55+ communities with resort-style amenities.

St. Petersburg is a vibrant waterfront city in Pinellas County, known for its arts scene, diverse neighborhoods, and Gulf Coast lifestyle. Often called the "Sunshine City," St. Pete has undergone a dramatic transformation over the past decade, becoming one of the most sought-after housing markets in Florida.

Below is a data-driven breakdown of what is happening in the St. Petersburg housing market right now, what it means for buyers and sellers, and where prices are headed through the rest of 2026.

What Is Driving the St. Petersburg Housing Market?

  • Arts, culture, and lifestyle driving relocation demand. St. Petersburg has transformed into one of Florida's most desirable cities, earning comparisons to Austin and Portland. The Dali Museum, SHINE mural festival, thriving dining scene, and waterfront parks draw relocating professionals and remote workers. This lifestyle premium sustains demand across all price points.
  • Downtown revitalization and condo development. Billions in development investment are reshaping downtown St. Pete with new condo towers, hotel projects, and mixed-use developments. The Tropicana Field redevelopment project alone represents a transformative investment that will add housing, retail, and office space to the urban core.
  • Waterfront premium in a land-constrained market. St. Petersburg is a peninsula city with water on three sides. You cannot create more waterfront land, which creates a permanent supply constraint. St. Petersburg offers opportunities across a wide price spectrum, from 0K condos in midtown to M+ waterfront properties. Inventory has improved, but desirable neighborhoods like Old Northeast, Kenwood, and the Grand Central District remain competitive. Come pre-approved and be ready to act. The condo market offers the most inventory and the best negotiating position, particularly in buildings with older condo associations facing special assessments.

What Do Current Conditions Mean for Sellers?

St. Petersburg sellers benefit from continued strong demand, but the market has shifted toward realistic pricing. The era of listing high and waiting for an overpay is over. Price at comparable sales, invest in staging and photography, and your home will move. Waterfront and walkable-to-downtown properties still generate the most competition. If you are in a condo building with pending special assessments, address this transparently in your listing.

St. Petersburg Housing Market Forecast: Rest of 2026

St. Petersburg home prices are projected to rise 4-6% through 2026. The city benefits from multiple tailwinds: lifestyle appeal, limited land supply, downtown redevelopment, and ongoing demographic shifts favoring Sun Belt cities. The Tropicana Field redevelopment will be a significant catalyst over the next 3-5 years. Risk factors include rising insurance costs and condo association special assessments, particularly in older waterfront buildings.

Frequently Asked Questions About the St. Petersburg Housing Market

Is St. Petersburg FL a good place to buy a home?

St. Petersburg is one of the most desirable markets in Tampa Bay. The combination of arts/culture, waterfront living, walkable neighborhoods, and strong appreciation makes it attractive for both primary residence and investment buyers. The challenge is finding the right property at the right price in this competitive market.

What are the best neighborhoods in St. Petersburg?

Popular neighborhoods include Old Northeast (historic charm, walkability), Downtown/EDGE District (urban living, restaurants), Kenwood (bungalows, arts community), Shore Acres (waterfront, mid-century homes), and Snell Isle (upscale waterfront). Each has a distinct personality and price range.

How much does it cost to live in St. Petersburg?

The median home price is 0,000, with significant variation by neighborhood. A comfortable household income for homeownership in St. Pete starts around ,000-0,000 for a median-priced home with conventional financing. Waterfront and downtown areas require substantially more.

Is St. Petersburg better than Tampa?

It depends on your priorities. St. Petersburg offers more walkability, a stronger arts/culture scene, and beach proximity. Tampa offers more job diversity, larger suburbs, and generally lower prices for equivalent square footage. Many residents consider them complementary rather than competitive.

Are condos a good investment in St. Petersburg?

Condos in St. Petersburg can be strong investments, but due diligence is critical. Check the association's reserve fund, upcoming special assessments, and insurance costs. Post-Surfside legislation has increased financial requirements for condo associations, which has led to special assessments in some older buildings. Newer buildings and well-managed associations remain solid investments.

Temple Terrace is an independent incorporated city within Hillsborough County, not part of the City of Tampa. It has its own mayor, city council, police department, and municipal services. Despite its proximity to Tampa, Temple Terrace maintains its own civic identity and governance.

  • Seasonal timing matters. Sun City Center has a strong seasonal buyer pattern. January through April (snowbird season) generates the highest buyer traffic. Listing during this window maximizes exposure.

content:

The Lutz housing market in Q1 2026 shows a median sale price of approximately $500,000, up 4.6% year-over-year. Homes are selling in a median 33 days, with demand strong for larger-lot properties in gated communities. Sellers are averaging 97.2% of list price at closing.

What Is Driving the Lutz Market Right Now?

Three forces are shaping the Q1 2026 market in Lutz:

  • Larger lots and gated communities drive premium pricing. Lutz is known for half-acre to multi-acre properties in communities like Cheval, Heritage Isles, and Lake St. Charles. Buyers seeking space, privacy, and upscale amenities without the South Tampa price tag gravitate toward Lutz.
  • Dual-county positioning offers school choice. Lutz straddles the Hillsborough-Pasco county line, giving buyers access to school options in both counties. Steinbrenner High School on the Hillsborough side is particularly sought after.
  • Veterans Expressway and Suncoast Parkway access. Lutz benefits from direct highway access to Tampa, the airport, and Pasco County employment centers. The Suncoast Parkway extension has improved connectivity for northern Lutz properties.

Home Prices by Property Type

Single-Family (3BR/2BA)$450,000$370K - $550K1,800
Single-Family (4BR/3BA)$565,000$470K - $700K2,500

Luxury / Estate ($800K+)$950,000$800K - $1.5M3,800

Buyer Conditions: What to Expect in Q1 2026

At 2.6 months of supply, the Lutz market still favors sellers in most price ranges. Here is what buyers should expect:

  • Hillsborough vs. Pasco side matters. Properties on the Hillsborough County side of Lutz generally command 5-10% premiums over comparable Pasco-side homes, primarily due to school zone preferences. Verify which county your target property falls in.
  • Well and septic are common on larger lots. Many Lutz properties on half-acre+ lots use well water and septic systems. Budget for inspections and understand long-term maintenance requirements.
  • Gated community HOA fees vary widely. Monthly HOA fees in Lutz communities range from $100 to $400+ depending on amenities. Factor this into your total housing cost analysis.
  • Competition in the $450K-$550K range. This price range attracts the most buyer activity in Lutz, with well-priced homes generating multiple offers within the first two weeks.

Seller Conditions: Pricing Strategy Matters More Than Ever

Sellers in Lutz are in a favorable position, but the margin for error on pricing has narrowed. The days of listing 10% above market and getting full-price offers are over.

  • Market to the right buyer profile. Lutz buyers are typically move-up purchasers or relocators seeking space, schools, and a semi-rural suburban feel. Emphasize lot size, outdoor living areas, and community amenities in your marketing.
  • Luxury properties need patience and precision. Homes above $800,000 average 45-55 days on market. These require premium photography, virtual tours, and targeted marketing to reach qualified buyers.
  • Price correctly from day one. Lutz's smaller buyer pool at higher price points means overpricing is punished with extended market time. Work with comparable sales data, not aspirational pricing.

Barrett Henry's listing strategy for Lutz sellers includes a comprehensive market analysis, professional photography, targeted digital marketing, and strategic pricing designed to generate strong offers within the first two weeks on market.

Lutz Market Forecast: What to Expect Through 2026

Based on current data and trends, here is Barrett Henry's outlook for the Lutz market through the remainder of 2026:

  • Prices: Expect 3-5% appreciation. Lutz's desirable lot sizes and gated-community appeal provide steady demand support.
  • Inventory: Supply remains limited, particularly for properties on one acre or more. New construction in planned communities adds some inventory but cannot replicate the established lot sizes in original Lutz.
  • Rates: Rate decreases would benefit Lutz's higher-price market segment, bringing move-up buyers who are currently locked in at lower rates.
  • Risk factors: Insurance costs for larger properties and older homes continue to escalate. Buyers should also consider the potential impact of Pasco County growth on traffic patterns along US-41 and SR-54. Read the full insurance guide here.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the average home price in Lutz FL?

As of Q1 2026, the median sale price for homes in Lutz is approximately $500,000. Prices range from the $220,000s for condos and townhomes to over $1.5 million for estate properties on acreage. The median price per square foot is $240.

Is Lutz FL a good place to live?

Lutz offers a blend of suburban and semi-rural living with larger lots, gated communities, and good school access in both Hillsborough and Pasco counties. The area appeals to families wanting space without sacrificing highway access to Tampa. Read the full Lutz community guide.

How fast are homes selling in Lutz?

The median days on market in Lutz is 33 days as of Q1 2026. Homes in the $450K-$550K sweet spot sell in around 26 days, while luxury properties above $800,000 average 45-55 days.

Is Lutz in Hillsborough or Pasco County?

Lutz straddles both Hillsborough and Pasco counties. Properties south of the county line (roughly Van Dyke Road area) are in Hillsborough County, while properties to the north are in Pasco. This distinction affects school assignments, tax rates, and county services.

What are the best neighborhoods in Lutz?

Top Lutz neighborhoods include Cheval (gated with golf course and spa), Heritage Isles (gated with resort amenities), Lake St. Charles (lakefront homesites), and the Lutz Lake Fern area (large lots, equestrian-friendly). Each offers a different lifestyle and price point. See the full neighborhood guide.

What Is Driving the Carrollwood Market Right Now?

Three forces are shaping the Q1 2026 market in Carrollwood:

  • Established neighborhoods command premiums. Carrollwood and Carrollwood Village offer mature landscaping, lakefront lots, country club amenities, and a residential character that newer subdivisions cannot replicate. Buyers pay a premium for the established community feel and tree-canopy streets.
  • Northwest Tampa location is central to everything. Carrollwood sits at the crossroads of Dale Mabry, Busch Boulevard, and Veterans Expressway, providing quick access to Tampa International Airport, Westshore business district, downtown Tampa, and the beaches. Location versatility drives consistent demand.
  • Strong school zones support family demand. The area's school zones, including access to several magnet and charter school options, keep Carrollwood competitive with east Hillsborough alternatives for families prioritizing education.

Home Prices by Property Type

Buyer Conditions: What to Expect in Q1 2026

At 2.3 months of supply, the Carrollwood market still favors sellers in most price ranges. Here is what buyers should expect:

  • Original Carrollwood vs. Carrollwood Village. Original Carrollwood (generally south of Fletcher Avenue) offers older, more affordable homes on larger lots. Carrollwood Village (north of Fletcher) is a deed-restricted community with lakes, a country club, and higher price points. Know which area fits your needs.
  • Lake views add $50K to $150K. Properties directly on Carrollwood's chain of lakes command significant premiums. Lakefront homes move quickly and rarely sit more than 3 weeks when priced correctly.
  • Older homes may need updates. Much of Carrollwood was built in the 1970s-1980s. Budget for potential roof replacement, kitchen updates, or pool resurfacing when evaluating established properties.
  • HOA rules vary significantly. Carrollwood Village has active deed restrictions. Original Carrollwood areas may have minimal or no HOA oversight. Verify restrictions before purchasing.

Seller Conditions: Pricing Strategy Matters More Than Ever

Sellers in Carrollwood are in a favorable position, but the margin for error on pricing has narrowed. The days of listing 10% above market and getting full-price offers are over.

  • Highlight location advantages. Carrollwood's central positioning is its strongest selling point. Proximity to Tampa International Airport, Veterans Expressway, and major employment centers is worth emphasizing in every listing.
  • Lakefront sellers have leverage. Lakefront properties are scarce and in demand. If you own a lakefront home, you have negotiating strength, but still need to price within the recent comparable range.
  • Updated interiors sell faster. Buyers in the $480K+ range expect modern kitchens and bathrooms. Homes with original 1980s finishes sit longer and sell for less. Strategic updates before listing deliver strong returns.

Barrett Henry's listing strategy for Carrollwood sellers includes a comprehensive market analysis, professional photography, targeted digital marketing, and strategic pricing designed to generate strong offers within the first two weeks on market.

Carrollwood Market Forecast: What to Expect Through 2026

Based on current data and trends, here is Barrett Henry's outlook for the Carrollwood market through the remainder of 2026:

  • Prices: Expect 3-5% appreciation. Carrollwood's established character and location advantages provide a price floor that protects against downside risk.
  • Inventory: Supply remains constrained. Limited buildable land means almost no new construction, keeping resale homes as the only option. The lock-in effect further limits supply.
  • Rates: Rate decreases would bring sidelined move-up buyers back into the market, potentially creating competition in the $450K to $600K sweet spot.
  • Risk factors: Aging infrastructure in older sections of Carrollwood may present maintenance costs for buyers. Insurance rates for older roof structures are rising. Read the full insurance guide here.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the average home price in Carrollwood FL?

As of Q1 2026, the median sale price for homes in Carrollwood is approximately $480,000. Prices range from the $210,000s for condos and townhomes to over $1.3 million for lakefront luxury properties. The median price per square foot is $248.

Is Carrollwood a good neighborhood in Tampa?

Carrollwood is one of Tampa's most desirable established neighborhoods. The area offers mature tree canopies, lake-oriented living, strong community amenities, and a central location with easy access to Tampa International Airport, Dale Mabry retail, and major highways. Read the full Carrollwood community guide.

How fast are homes selling in Carrollwood?

The median days on market in Carrollwood is 30 days as of Q1 2026. Homes under $450,000 move quickly (around 24 days), lakefront properties sell in 20-25 days when priced correctly, and homes above $700,000 average 40-50 days.

Is Carrollwood in Tampa or unincorporated?

Carrollwood is technically an unincorporated community in Hillsborough County, though it carries a Tampa mailing address. Carrollwood Village is a planned community within the larger Carrollwood area. Both benefit from Hillsborough County services and Tampa-area amenities.

What schools serve Carrollwood?

Carrollwood is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools, with several well-regarded elementary, middle, and high school options. The area also provides access to multiple magnet and charter school programs. Specific school assignments depend on your exact address within the Carrollwood area.

What Is Driving the Apollo Beach Market Right Now?

Three forces are shaping the Q1 2026 market in Apollo Beach:

  • Waterfront access at attainable prices. Apollo Beach offers canal homes with Tampa Bay access at a fraction of South Tampa or Davis Islands waterfront pricing. Boaters and water enthusiasts find genuine deepwater canal properties starting in the $500,000s, compared to $1M+ elsewhere in the bay.
  • The Waterset community drives new-build demand. Waterset, a large master-planned community by Newland, continues to attract buyers with resort-style amenities, new construction options, and a family-oriented environment. It is one of the top-selling communities in Hillsborough County.
  • Proximity to Tampa with a coastal feel. Apollo Beach is only 30 minutes from downtown Tampa and 20 minutes from MacDill AFB, but feels like a distinct waterfront community. The Tampa Bay shoreline, marinas, and the Florida Aquarium's Beach Club add to the coastal lifestyle appeal.

Home Prices by Property Type

Property TypeMedian PricePrice RangeAvg Sq Ft
Single-Family (3BR/2BA)$385,000$310K - $465K1,650
Single-Family (4BR/3BA)$475,000$400K - $580K2,250
Townhome/Condo$275,000$210K - $350K1,350
Waterfront / Canal$625,000$500K - $1.2M2,400
New Construction (Waterset)$460,000$380K - $600K2,100

Buyer Conditions: What to Expect in Q1 2026

At 2.3 months of supply, the Apollo Beach market still favors sellers in most price ranges. Here is what buyers should expect:

  • Waterfront premiums are real but justified. Canal homes with Tampa Bay access command $150,000 to $300,000 premiums over comparable non-waterfront homes. Factor in dock condition, seawall age, and water depth when evaluating waterfront properties.
  • Flood insurance is a critical cost factor. Many Apollo Beach properties fall in flood zones AE or VE. Annual flood insurance can run $2,000 to $8,000 depending on elevation and zone. Always get a flood insurance quote before making an offer.
  • Waterset offers builder incentives. New construction in Waterset frequently includes rate buydowns, design center credits, and closing cost assistance. Compare builder packages carefully.
  • Seawall inspection is essential. For canal properties, seawall condition can represent a $30,000 to $80,000 replacement cost. Always include a seawall inspection contingency.

Seller Conditions: Pricing Strategy Matters More Than Ever

Sellers in Apollo Beach are in a favorable position, but the margin for error on pricing has narrowed. The days of listing 10% above market and getting full-price offers are over.

  • Waterfront sells itself, but pricing still matters. Canal and waterfront properties generate strong interest but are also more sensitive to overpricing due to smaller buyer pools. Price to recent comparable waterfront sales, not to wishful thinking.
  • Showcase the lifestyle. Professional photography that captures water views, dock areas, sunsets, and outdoor living spaces is essential. Waterfront buyers are buying a lifestyle as much as a structure.
  • Prepare for insurance questions. Buyers will ask about flood insurance costs, wind mitigation credits, and seawall condition. Have documentation ready to avoid delays.

Barrett Henry's listing strategy for Apollo Beach sellers includes a comprehensive market analysis, professional photography, targeted digital marketing, and strategic pricing designed to generate strong offers within the first two weeks on market.

Apollo Beach Market Forecast: What to Expect Through 2026

Based on current data and trends, here is Barrett Henry's outlook for the Apollo Beach market through the remainder of 2026:

  • Prices: Expect 3-5% appreciation overall, with waterfront properties potentially outperforming as Tampa Bay waterfront inventory remains scarce at attainable price points.
  • Inventory: Waterset will continue delivering new construction inventory, but existing canal-front homes will remain scarce. Waterfront supply is inherently limited.
  • Rates: Rate drops would disproportionately benefit Apollo Beach's higher price points, bringing more buyers into the $500K+ waterfront segment.
  • Risk factors: Rising flood insurance costs and climate-related concerns about sea level are long-term factors for waterfront properties. Buyers should evaluate elevation certificates and insurance costs as part of total housing cost analysis. Read the full insurance guide here.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the average home price in Apollo Beach FL?

As of Q1 2026, the median sale price for homes in Apollo Beach is approximately $425,000. Non-waterfront homes range from the $210,000s for condos to $580,000+ for larger single-family properties. Canal and waterfront homes range from $500,000 to over $1.2 million. The median price per square foot is $232.

Is Apollo Beach FL a good place to buy?

Apollo Beach offers a unique combination of waterfront living, new construction options in Waterset, and proximity to Tampa. For buyers who want boat access to Tampa Bay without South Tampa prices, Apollo Beach is one of the best values on the water in the entire Tampa Bay area. Read the full Apollo Beach community guide.

How fast are homes selling in Apollo Beach?

The median days on market in Apollo Beach is 34 days as of Q1 2026. Standard homes in Waterset and non-waterfront areas sell faster (around 28 days), while waterfront canal homes average 40-50 days due to their higher price points and more specialized buyer pool.

Does Apollo Beach flood?

Some areas of Apollo Beach are in designated flood zones, particularly properties closest to Tampa Bay and the canal systems. Flood zone designation varies by property. An elevation certificate and flood zone determination are essential parts of due diligence. Flood insurance is required for properties in high-risk zones with federally backed mortgages.

Is Apollo Beach a good investment?

Apollo Beach has shown consistent appreciation, particularly for waterfront properties where supply is inherently limited. The combination of Waterset's ongoing development, waterfront scarcity, and proximity to Tampa supports long-term value. Rental demand is strong for both long-term and seasonal tenants.

The area combines semi-rural character with top-tier schools, making it a magnet for families willing to pay a premium for the best public school assignments in the county.

  • Top-rated schools driving family demand. Lithia is zoned for some of the highest-rated schools in Hillsborough County, including Bevis Elementary, Barrington Middle, and Newsome High School. The main risk is affordability -- as median prices approach $500K, first-time families may redirect to more affordable alternatives like Riverview or Wimauma.

Is Lithia FL a good place to live?

Lithia is one of the most sought-after communities in Hillsborough County, particularly for families. A-rated schools, master-planned communities like FishHawk Ranch, natural beauty, and a semi-rural atmosphere make it consistently popular. The trade-off is higher prices and a longer commute to central Tampa.

What is the difference between Lithia and FishHawk?

FishHawk Ranch is a master-planned community located within the Lithia area. Lithia is the broader geographic area that includes FishHawk plus surrounding neighborhoods, rural properties, and smaller subdivisions. FishHawk has specific amenities, HOA requirements, and CDD assessments. Lithia outside of FishHawk offers more variety in lot sizes and pricing.

How are schools in Lithia FL?

Lithia has some of the top-rated schools in Hillsborough County. Bevis Elementary, Barrington Middle, and Newsome High School are all highly rated. The school zone is one of the primary reasons families choose Lithia over other Hillsborough communities.

How far is Lithia from Tampa?

Lithia is approximately 25 miles southeast of downtown Tampa. Commute times average 35-45 minutes via Lithia Pinecrest Road to I-75. Brandon and Riverview are about 15 minutes away.

Are there rural properties available in Lithia?

Yes. Outside of FishHawk and other master-planned communities, Lithia offers properties on 1-5+ acres with agricultural zoning. These properties attract buyers seeking space for horses, hobby farming, or simply a more private setting. Rural Lithia properties are increasingly rare and command premiums.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Longboat Key FL a good place to buy a home in 2026?

Longboat Key is one of the premier luxury barrier island communities on Florida's Gulf Coast. It spans both Manatee and Sarasota counties and is known for its upscale condominiums, golf communities, and pristine beaches. The buyer profile skews toward retirees, second-home owners, and high-net-worth individuals. Prices are among the highest in the Tampa Bay-Sarasota corridor, but the quality of life and exclusivity support the premium.

How much does a house cost on Longboat Key FL?

Longboat Key home prices range from the mid-$500s for older condominiums to $5M+ for Gulf-front estates. The median sale price typically falls between $800K and $1.5M depending on the mix of condo vs. single-family sales in a given quarter. The north end of the key (Manatee County side) tends to have more condos at lower price points, while the south end (Sarasota County) features larger single-family estates. Contact Barrett Henry for current Longboat Key listings.

Is Longboat Key safe from hurricanes?

Longboat Key faces the same hurricane risks as all Gulf Coast barrier islands. The key is long and narrow, making it particularly vulnerable to storm surge. Mandatory evacuations are ordered for barrier islands during major hurricane threats, and the single bridge access points (at each end) can create evacuation bottlenecks. Hurricane Ian in 2022 caused damage to parts of the key. Flood insurance is required and expensive. Buyers should factor hurricane risk and insurance costs into every Longboat Key purchase decision.

What are the pros and cons of living on Longboat Key?

The pros are spectacular beaches, a quiet and exclusive atmosphere, excellent golf at the Longboat Key Club, low crime, and a strong sense of community among residents. The cons are high home prices, expensive insurance, limited dining and shopping (most residents go to Sarasota or Bradenton for errands), bridge-dependent access, and seasonal population swings — the key is notably quieter May through November. Longboat Key is ideal for retirees and second-home buyers who value peace and quality over convenience.

Is Longboat Key a good investment?

Longboat Key has historically appreciated well due to severe supply constraints, high barriers to entry, and consistent demand from affluent buyers. The luxury end of the market can be volatile — high-end properties may take longer to sell but tend to recover and appreciate over time. The investment risk factors are rising insurance costs, hurricane exposure, and the potential impact of climate concerns on barrier island values. For buyers with a long-term horizon, Longboat Key remains one of the Gulf Coast's strongest luxury markets.

How far is Longboat Key from Sarasota?

Longboat Key stretches about 10 miles from the north end (near Bradenton Beach) to the south end (near Lido Key). The south end is just minutes from St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota — roughly 10-15 minutes. The north end is closer to Bradenton at about 15-20 minutes. Tampa is approximately 60-75 minutes from the north end of Longboat Key via I-75 or US 41.

What is the Longboat Key Club?

The Longboat Key Club is a private resort and residential community on the south end of Longboat Key. It features two 18-hole golf courses, tennis facilities, a private beach, marina, and multiple dining options. Real estate within the club ranges from condos to custom waterfront homes. Membership is available to property owners and offers a resort-style lifestyle that is central to the Longboat Key appeal for many buyers.

Is Anna Maria Island a good place to buy a home in 2026?

Anna Maria Island is one of the most desirable — and most expensive — beach communities on Florida's Gulf Coast. The island enforces strict building codes that preserve its Old Florida character, including height restrictions that prevent high-rise development. This creates a supply-constrained market where well-maintained properties hold value exceptionally well. The tradeoff is price: entry points start around $700K and Gulf-front homes routinely exceed $2M.

How much does a house cost on Anna Maria Island?

Home prices on Anna Maria Island range from roughly $700K for smaller cottages and bay-side properties to over $3M for Gulf-front homes in the City of Anna Maria. The median sale price typically falls between $900K and $1.3M depending on the quarter. Holmes Beach and Bradenton Beach (the other two cities on the island) offer slightly lower entry points than the City of Anna Maria. Contact Barrett Henry for current inventory and pricing.

Can you do vacation rentals on Anna Maria Island?

Vacation rental regulations on Anna Maria Island vary by city. The City of Anna Maria has some of the strictest short-term rental rules on the island, while Holmes Beach and Bradenton Beach have different ordinances. Rental income potential is a major driver of property values island-wide, but the regulatory landscape has been contentious. Always verify current rental rules for the specific city and zoning district before purchasing with investment intent.

Is Anna Maria Island safe from hurricanes?

No barrier island in Florida is safe from hurricanes. Anna Maria Island is vulnerable to storm surge, which is the primary threat during a major hurricane. The island's low elevation means even a Category 1 or 2 storm could cause significant flooding. Mandatory evacuation orders are common during hurricane threats. Flood insurance is required for mortgaged properties and essential for cash buyers. The island has weathered many storms, but the risk is real and should be factored into every purchase decision.

What makes Anna Maria Island different from other Florida beaches?

Anna Maria Island stands out because of its enforced Old Florida character. Height restrictions (typically 3 stories max), no chain restaurants in the City of Anna Maria, and a deliberately low-key atmosphere set it apart from commercialized beach towns. Pine Avenue in the City of Anna Maria has a walkable village feel with independent shops and restaurants. The island attracts buyers who are specifically seeking the opposite of a Clearwater Beach or Miami Beach experience.

Is Anna Maria Island a good investment?

Anna Maria Island has historically delivered strong appreciation due to its severe supply constraints and enduring demand. The building height restrictions and limited developable land mean new inventory rarely comes online, which supports pricing. Rental income adds to the investment case. The risks are insurance costs (rising across all Florida barrier islands), hurricane exposure, and regulatory uncertainty around short-term rentals. For buyers with a long-term horizon and the budget to absorb insurance costs, AMI has been a reliable store of value.

How far is Anna Maria Island from Tampa?

Anna Maria Island is approximately 50-60 miles from downtown Tampa, which translates to about a 60-75 minute drive via I-275 and US 41. Sarasota is closer at roughly 30 minutes. The Manatee Avenue bridge (SR 64) connects the island to the mainland at Bradenton. This distance from Tampa makes AMI less practical for daily commuters but ideal for retirees, remote workers, and second-home buyers.

Davenport works well for full-time residents who want theme park access and newer construction at competitive prices. What are the pros and cons of living in Davenport FL?

The biggest pros are affordable newer homes, Disney proximity, resort-style community amenities, and access to both Tampa and Orlando via I-4. Is it a buyers or sellers market in Davenport right now?

Should I buy in Davenport or Kissimmee?

Kissimmee is closer to Disney's main gates while Davenport properties tend to be newer and have better resort amenities. For vacation rentals, both markets perform well. For primary residence living, Kissimmee offers more walkability and urban convenience.

How much is homeowners insurance in Davenport FL?

Homeowners insurance in Davenport typically costs $1,800 to $4,000 per year for primary residences and can run higher for vacation rental properties due to increased liability. Davenport is inland, so flood insurance is generally not required. Newer construction with modern building codes gets the most favorable rates. Is Lake Wales FL a good place to retire?

Lake Wales is an excellent retirement destination for buyers who want affordable living, natural beauty, and a slower pace. Bok Tower Gardens, the Lake Wales Ridge, and numerous freshwater lakes provide outdoor recreation without the crowds of coastal communities. Healthcare is accessible through nearby Lakeland and Winter Haven medical centers. The low cost of living stretches retirement income further than most Florida locations.

What are the pros and cons of living in Lake Wales FL?

The biggest pros are low home prices, natural beauty along the Lake Wales Ridge, Bok Tower Gardens, and a revitalizing downtown. Are homes in Lake Wales a good investment?

Should I buy in Lake Wales or Winter Haven?

Lake Wales offers lower prices and more acreage, while Winter Haven has a more established downtown, the Chain of Lakes, and better proximity to Lakeland and I-4. If you want maximum affordability and do not mind being farther from major employment centers, Lake Wales is the better value. Frequently Asked Questions

Is Land O' Lakes FL a good place to live?

Land O' Lakes is one of the top-rated suburbs in the Tampa Bay area, particularly for families. It offers newer master-planned communities, good schools, abundant parks and nature preserves, and a suburban feel with reasonable access to Tampa. The area along the Suncoast Parkway corridor has seen explosive growth, adding new retail, dining, and medical facilities in recent years.

How much does a house cost in Land O' Lakes FL?

Home prices in Land O' Lakes typically range from $300,000 to $600,000 for most single-family homes. Newer construction in communities like Bexley and Connerton starts in the mid-$300s, while established neighborhoods like Lake Padgett offer larger lots at varied price points. Luxury acreage properties can exceed $1 million. For current data, see the pricing section above or contact Barrett Henry.

What are the pros and cons of living in Land O' Lakes FL?

Pros include affordable new construction, lower Pasco County property taxes, family-friendly communities, and access to nature preserves and outdoor recreation. Cons include a 30-45 minute commute to downtown Tampa, CDD fees in most newer communities, limited nightlife and dining compared to urban Tampa, and a car-dependent lifestyle. The Suncoast Parkway toll costs add up for daily commuters.

Is Land O' Lakes FL a good place to raise a family?

Land O' Lakes is one of the top family-friendly areas in Pasco County. The area offers highly rated schools, safe neighborhoods, and an abundance of parks and nature preserves. Master-planned communities like Bexley and Connerton are specifically designed with families in mind, featuring playgrounds, community pools, and organized events. The combination of suburban convenience and natural beauty makes it a strong choice for families.

Are property taxes high in Land O' Lakes FL?

Property taxes in Land O' Lakes fall under Pasco County rates, which are generally lower than Hillsborough County. However, many master-planned communities have CDD fees on top of property taxes, ranging from $1,500 to $4,000+ annually. These fees fund infrastructure and amenities within the community. Barrett Henry can provide a complete tax and fee breakdown for any property you are considering.

How far is Land O' Lakes from Tampa?

Land O' Lakes is approximately 25-35 minutes from downtown Tampa, depending on your specific neighborhood and traffic conditions. The Suncoast Parkway and Veterans Expressway provide direct highway access south into Tampa and Hillsborough County. Communities along the Suncoast Parkway corridor tend to have the fastest commute times, though toll costs are a factor for daily commuters.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is St. Pete Beach a good place to buy a home in 2026?

St. Pete Beach is one of Florida's premier Gulf Coast beach destinations, consistently ranked among the best beaches in the country. The market is competitive, with strong demand from both full-time residents and vacation rental investors. Pass-a-Grille on the south end offers a quiet, historic village feel, while the central stretch near the Don CeSar has a resort atmosphere. Prices reflect the prestige — this is not an affordable beach market, but it is a proven one for long-term value.

How much does a house cost in St. Pete Beach FL?

St. Pete Beach home prices range from the low $400s for older condos to over $3M for Gulf-front homes in Pass-a-Grille. The median sale price typically falls between $600K and $1M, though it fluctuates based on the mix of condo vs. single-family closings. The south end (Pass-a-Grille) commands the highest single-family prices, while the central and north sections offer more condo inventory at varied price points. Contact Barrett Henry for current St. Pete Beach listings.

Can you do vacation rentals in St. Pete Beach?

St. Pete Beach allows vacation rentals, and rental income is a major component of the local real estate market. The city regulates short-term rentals through a resort tax and registration system. Condos along Gulf Boulevard are popular rental properties, particularly during the January-April peak season. Always verify current rules, HOA restrictions, and licensing requirements before purchasing with rental income as your primary investment thesis.

How does St. Pete Beach compare to Clearwater Beach?

St. Pete Beach and Clearwater Beach are the two marquee Gulf beach communities in the Tampa Bay area. Clearwater Beach is more commercialized with large resorts and a busier tourist scene. St. Pete Beach — particularly Pass-a-Grille — offers a more laid-back, residential feel with less high-rise density. Prices are comparable in the premium segments, though Clearwater Beach tends to have more condo inventory. Both face similar hurricane, flood, and insurance considerations.

Does St. Pete Beach flood?

Yes. St. Pete Beach is a barrier island community with significant flood exposure. All sections of the beach are in FEMA flood zones, and flood insurance is required for mortgaged properties. Storm surge during hurricanes is the primary risk, and the island is in the mandatory evacuation zone for most tropical storm and hurricane events. Insurance costs have risen substantially and are a major factor in the total cost of ownership for any St. Pete Beach property.

What is Pass-a-Grille in St. Pete Beach?

Pass-a-Grille is the historic south end of St. Pete Beach and one of the most charming beach neighborhoods in Florida. It features a walkable grid of streets, the Hurricane restaurant, independent shops, and some of the widest beaches on the Gulf Coast. Pass-a-Grille properties command premium prices due to limited supply, no high-rise development, and a devoted community that fights to preserve its village character. It is the most sought-after address on St. Pete Beach.

Are home prices going up in St. Pete Beach?

St. Pete Beach home prices have appreciated steadily, supported by limited supply, strong tourism-driven demand, and national recognition as a top U.S. beach destination. Price growth moderated from the 2021-2022 peak but remains positive. Rising insurance costs are the primary headwind for all barrier island markets. Frequently Asked Questions

Is Gulfport FL a good place to buy a home in 2026?

Gulfport is one of Tampa Bay's most underrated communities for homebuyers in 2026. This small waterfront city (population ~12,000) bordering St. Petersburg offers an artsy, LGBTQ-friendly village atmosphere with a walkable downtown, independent restaurants, and weekly events like the Tuesday Fresh Market. Home prices remain below St. Petersburg and the barrier islands, making Gulfport a strong value play for buyers who want character and Boca Ciega Bay access at a reasonable price.

How much does a house cost in Gulfport FL?

Gulfport home prices typically range from the mid-$200s for smaller bungalows further from the waterfront to $700K+ for canal-front and bay-view properties. The median sale price generally falls in the $350K-$450K range, which represents significant value compared to neighboring St. Petersburg. The downtown Gulfport area and canal streets near Shore Acres command the highest premiums. Contact Barrett Henry for current Gulfport listings and pricing.

What is Gulfport FL known for?

Gulfport is known for its vibrant arts community, LGBTQ-friendly culture, and quirky small-town character. The city hosts regular events including the Tuesday Fresh Market, Art Walk, and Gecko Festival. The downtown waterfront along Beach Boulevard features independent galleries, restaurants, bars, and the historic Gulfport Casino (a community event venue, not a gambling establishment). Stetson University College of Law is also located in Gulfport.

Is Gulfport FL safe?

Gulfport is generally a safe community with an active local police department and strong neighborhood engagement. Crime rates track similarly to surrounding areas of south Pinellas County. Like any urban-adjacent community, safety varies by block — the areas near downtown and the waterfront tend to be well-patrolled and well-maintained. The small-city feel and engaged resident base contribute to a watchful community atmosphere.

Does Gulfport FL flood?

Gulfport sits on Boca Ciega Bay, and properties near the waterfront, along the canals, and in low-lying areas do face flood risk. Some parts of Gulfport are in FEMA-designated flood zones, which means flood insurance is required for mortgaged properties in those areas. Inland properties on higher ground are often outside flood zones. The city has invested in stormwater infrastructure improvements, but bay-side flooding during heavy rain and storm surge events remains a concern for waterfront properties.

Is Gulfport cheaper than St. Petersburg?

Yes. Gulfport home prices typically run 15-30% below comparable properties in popular St. Petersburg neighborhoods. You can find waterfront-access homes in Gulfport for prices that would only buy an inland property in St. Pete. The tradeoff is a smaller city with fewer big-city amenities, but many buyers consider that a feature rather than a bug. Gulfport's proximity to St. Pete (it borders the city) means you get easy access to St. Pete's restaurants, shops, and cultural venues anyway.

What are the pros and cons of living in Gulfport FL?

The pros are affordability relative to St. Pete and the beaches, a walkable downtown with genuine character, bay access, a strong arts and events scene, and a welcoming community culture. The cons include some flood zone exposure near the waterfront, a smaller commercial base (you will drive to St. Pete for many errands), and some blocks with deferred maintenance. Gulfport is ideal for buyers who value authenticity and community over polish and proximity to Gulf beaches.

Can you do short-term rentals in Indian Rocks Beach?

Is Indian Rocks Beach a good investment?

Barrier island properties across Tampa Bay have appreciated well over time. The risks are insurance costs, hurricane exposure, and potential regulatory changes on short-term rentals. For buyers who can weather the insurance burden, the combination of rental income potential and long-term appreciation makes IRB compelling.

How far is Indian Rocks Beach from Tampa?

Indian Rocks Beach is approximately 25-30 miles from downtown Tampa, which translates to a 35-50 minute commute depending on traffic and your route. Most commuters use the Courtney Campbell Causeway or SR 60 (Gulf-to-Bay). While not an ideal daily commute, many IRB residents work in Clearwater, Largo, or Pinellas Park, which are all within 10-20 minutes.

Is Pinellas Park cheaper than St. Petersburg?

Is Tarpon Springs FL a good place to buy a home in 2026?

Home prices tend to run below Palm Harbor and Dunedin, making it attractive for buyers who want a Pinellas address without premium pricing. See our best neighborhoods in Tarpon Springs for area-by-area pricing.

How much does a house cost in Tarpon Springs FL?

Tarpon Springs home prices range from the low $300s in more established neighborhoods to $700K+ for waterfront properties along the Anclote River and Spring Bayou. The median sale price typically falls in the low-to-mid $400s. Greektown and the Sponge Docks area command premiums for their walkability and charm, while the Keystone/Woodfield area offers larger lots at moderate prices. Contact Barrett Henry for current pricing in your target area.

Is Tarpon Springs safe from hurricanes?

No coastal Florida city is completely safe from hurricanes, but Tarpon Springs is positioned on the northern edge of Pinellas County with some natural protection from Anclote Key and the barrier islands to the west. The primary risks are storm surge near the waterfront and the Anclote River, plus wind damage from any major storm tracking through Tampa Bay. Inland neighborhoods like Cypress Run and Woodfield face less flood risk than waterfront areas. Flood insurance is recommended and often required near the coast.

What makes Tarpon Springs different from other Florida beach towns?

Tarpon Springs stands apart because of its living Greek-American heritage. The Sponge Docks area is not a tourist gimmick — it is a working waterfront with authentic Greek restaurants, bakeries, and a commercial sponge industry that dates back over a century. The Epiphany celebration draws national attention each January. This cultural identity gives Tarpon Springs a sense of place that most Florida communities lack, and it drives steady tourism dollars that support local businesses.

Does Tarpon Springs flood?

Always pull a flood zone determination for any specific property before purchasing.

Is Tarpon Springs FL expensive?

Tarpon Springs is moderately priced compared to other Pinellas County waterfront communities. It is generally more affordable than Dunedin, Palm Harbor, and Clearwater Beach while offering similar Gulf-side living. Property taxes in Pinellas County are among the higher rates in Florida, which is worth factoring into your total housing cost. Florida has no state income tax, which partially offsets the property tax burden for buyers relocating from income-tax states.

What are the pros and cons of living in Tarpon Springs?

The pros include a unique cultural identity, waterfront access, below-average Pinellas home prices, and strong community character. The cons are a longer commute to Tampa (40-50 minutes), limited nightlife outside the Sponge Docks, some flood zone exposure, and aging infrastructure in older neighborhoods. Tarpon Springs is ideal for buyers who prioritize character and value over proximity to urban amenities.

Year-over-year appreciation has settled into a healthy 2-4% range — a significant cooling from the double-digit spikes of 2021-2022, but exactly the kind of sustainable growth that builds long-term equity without pricing out the next wave of buyers.

Several factors are shaping this market right now:

  • Inventory recovery is real but gradual. Active listings have increased roughly 18-22% compared to the same period in 2026, but we are still well below the pre-pandemic norms of 2018-2019. This means buyers have more options than last year, but the market is not flooded.
  • Interest rates remain the single biggest variable. With conventional 30-year rates hovering in the mid-6% range as of March 2026, affordability is the conversation every buyer is having. Rate movement in either direction will have an outsized impact on transaction volume here.
  • Carrollwood's location premium keeps strengthening. Proximity to Tampa International Airport, Dale Mabry Highway, the Veterans Expressway, and downtown Tampa gives this community a commute advantage that newer suburbs further north simply cannot match.
  • No CDD fees in most established neighborhoods. This is a significant cost advantage that many buyers overlook when comparing Carrollwood to newer developments in Pasco or eastern Hillsborough County where Community Development District assessments can add $2,000-$4,000 or more per year to ownership costs.

If you want to understand how these trends played out last year, the 2025 Carrollwood housing market report provides useful baseline context. The shift from 2025 to 2026 has been more evolutionary than revolutionary — and that is exactly what a mature, well-located market should look like.

The sale-to-list ratio at 97.7% tells us that sellers are getting close to asking price on average, but the days of routinely selling 3-5% over list are behind us. Buyers have more negotiating power than they did in 2022 or 2023, but this is still a market where correctly priced homes sell near full value.

Price Ranges — Where the Activity Is

The sweet spot for buyer activity in Carrollwood right now sits between $375,000 and $525,000. This range captures the majority of move-up buyers, relocating professionals, and families looking for established neighborhoods with strong school zoning. Homes priced under $400,000 tend to sell fastest, often within 10-14 days. If you are specifically looking in that range, the Carrollwood homes under $500K page is updated regularly with available options.

Properties above $600,000 are taking longer to sell — typically 45-65 days — but are still moving when priced in line with comparable sales. The luxury end of the market, particularly lakefront properties and larger lots in Carrollwood Village, continues to see strong demand from cash buyers and those relocating from higher-cost states.

Carrollwood Village vs Greater Carrollwood — Market Differences

One of the most common questions I get from buyers and even from agents unfamiliar with the area is about the difference between Carrollwood Village and Greater Carrollwood. The distinction matters because it directly impacts pricing, HOA requirements, and long-term value retention.

Carrollwood Village

Carrollwood Village is a deed-restricted community with an active homeowners association that enforces architectural standards, maintains common areas, and operates community amenities including a country club and golf course. Homes in the Village tend to be larger on average, sitting on more generous lots, and the deed restrictions help protect property values by maintaining neighborhood aesthetics.

In spring 2026, median prices in Carrollwood Village are running approximately $510,000-$545,000, with Village listings showing strong demand particularly for updated homes with modern kitchens and renovated owners suites. The premium over Greater Carrollwood has widened slightly — Village homes command roughly 12-18% more than comparable-sized homes in non-Village sections.

Greater Carrollwood

Greater Carrollwood encompasses the broader unincorporated area surrounding the Village. It includes a wide variety of neighborhoods, price points, and property types. You will find everything from 1970s ranch homes on half-acre lots to newer infill construction from the 2000s and 2010s. Median prices in Greater Carrollwood are running $410,000-$445,000, making it significantly more accessible for first-time buyers and those wanting to be in the Carrollwood area without the Village price tag.

For a detailed breakdown of these two markets, the Carrollwood Village vs Carrollwood comparison guide walks through schools, amenities, HOA details, and neighborhood-by-neighborhood analysis.

Inventory and Days on Market — What Buyers and Sellers Should Know

Inventory is the metric that determines whether you are in a buyer's market, a seller's market, or somewhere in between. In Carrollwood as of March 2026, we are looking at approximately 2.8-3.2 months of supply across all property types. For context, 4-6 months is considered balanced. Below 4 months favors sellers. Above 6 months favors buyers.

So Carrollwood is still technically a seller's market, but it is a far cry from the sub-1-month supply we saw in early 2022. Buyers have breathing room. They can tour multiple homes, request inspections, and negotiate repairs without the panic-driven waiving of contingencies that defined the pandemic era.

The pattern is clear: the lower the price point, the faster homes sell. Entry-level homes under $350,000 — primarily condos, townhomes, and smaller single-family homes — are effectively being absorbed as fast as they list. If you are shopping in that range, you need to be pre-approved and ready to write offers within hours of a new listing hitting the MLS. Browse current options on the Carrollwood condos and townhomes page.

For sellers, the takeaway is that overpricing costs you more time and more money than it did two years ago. A home priced 5-7% above market value in 2022 might have still sold within 30 days. In spring 2026, that same overprice could mean 60-90 days on market, a price reduction, and ultimately selling for less than you would have gotten if you had priced correctly from the start. My selling guide for Carrollwood homeowners covers pricing strategy in detail.

Interest Rates and Their Impact on Carrollwood in 2026

Interest rates are the headline story of real estate in 2026 — not just in Carrollwood, but across the entire Florida housing market. As of March 2026, conventional 30-year fixed rates are hovering in the 6.25-6.75% range, roughly where they have been oscillating since late 2024. The Federal Reserve has signaled a cautious approach to further rate adjustments, and most economists are projecting rates to stay in this corridor through at least mid-2026.

Here is what this rate environment means in real dollars for a Carrollwood buyer:

The difference between 6.25% and 6.75% on a median-priced Carrollwood home is approximately $123 per month — or about $44,000 over the life of the loan. That is not insignificant, and it is why rate-lock timing and lender shopping are critical components of any buying strategy right now.

One thing I always tell buyers: do not try to time the rate market. If you find the right home at a price that works for your budget at today's rates, buy it. You can always refinance later if rates drop. You cannot go back and buy the home someone else already bought while you were waiting for a half-point rate decrease that may or may not materialize.

Who Is Buying in Carrollwood Right Now?

The buyer pool in Carrollwood is diverse, but a few distinct groups are driving the majority of transactions in early 2026.

Move-Up Buyers (35-50 Age Range)

This is the largest active buyer group. These are families who purchased their first home in areas like Town 'N Country, Citrus Park, or Seminole Heights five to eight years ago, built equity during the appreciation boom, and are now ready for more space, better schools, and a more established neighborhood. They are typically shopping in the $425,000-$575,000 range and prioritize homes with four bedrooms, a dedicated owners suite, updated kitchens, and fenced yards. The Carrollwood schools guide is one of the most-viewed pages on my site for a reason — school quality drives many of these buying decisions.

Out-of-State Relocations

Florida's population growth continues, and Carrollwood benefits from its proximity to Tampa International Airport and major employers. Buyers relocating from the Northeast, Midwest, and California are drawn to Carrollwood because it offers suburban living within a reasonable commute to downtown Tampa, Westshore business district, and the airport corridor. Many of these buyers are coming from markets where $468,000 buys them a fraction of what they get here, so they tend to be decisive and well-funded. For these buyers, the complete Carrollwood real estate guide provides the orientation they need.

Investors

Carrollwood's strong rental demand and stable appreciation make it attractive for buy-and-hold investors. Whether it is a single-family rental, a condo, or a small multifamily property, the numbers can work — especially in Greater Carrollwood where acquisition costs are lower. More on this in the investment properties section below.

Active Adults and Downsizers

Empty nesters selling larger homes in South Tampa or beach communities and looking for lower-maintenance living are finding value in Carrollwood's 55+ communities and single-story options. The area's medical infrastructure, proximity to shopping, and established neighborhood feel are strong draws for this demographic.

Curious whether Carrollwood is the right fit for your lifestyle? The pros and cons guide gives an honest assessment.

Carrollwood for Sellers — Is Now a Good Time to List?

The short answer: yes, with caveats. Spring 2026 is a good time to sell in Carrollwood, but the margin for error on pricing and presentation is much thinner than it was two or three years ago.

Why the Timing Works

  • Spring buying season is in full swing. March through June is historically the strongest period for home sales in Tampa Bay. Buyer activity picks up, families want to close before the next school year, and the weather cooperates for showings.
  • Equity positions are strong. If you bought before 2022, you have likely seen 25-45% appreciation on your home. Even 2022-2023 buyers are sitting on modest gains thanks to Carrollwood's steady trajectory.
  • Demand still outpaces supply. With inventory below 4 months, sellers retain an advantage — just not the overwhelming advantage of the pandemic frenzy.

What Sellers Need to Get Right

  • Pricing accuracy matters more than ever. The data shows that homes priced within 3% of market value sell in half the time of those priced 5%+ above. Work with an agent who knows Carrollwood at the neighborhood level — not someone pulling comps from across the county and calling it a day.
  • Condition is not optional. Buyers in 2026 are not waiving inspections. Deferred maintenance — roof age, plumbing condition, electrical panel issues — will come up during inspection and cost you at the negotiating table. Address known issues before listing or price accordingly.
  • Insurance readiness is a selling advantage. Florida's insurance market remains challenging. If you can provide a clean four-point inspection, a recent roof certification, and documentation of any wind mitigation features, you make it dramatically easier for buyers to get insured — and that can be the difference between your home and the next one. The Florida homeowners insurance guide explains why this matters so much right now.

If you are considering selling, the Carrollwood seller's guide walks through the entire process from pre-listing preparation to closing day.

Carrollwood for Buyers — Strategies That Work in 2026

Buying a home in Carrollwood in 2026 requires a different playbook than what worked in 2021 or even 2024. The market has more inventory, but desirable homes still move quickly. Rates are higher than the historic lows, but financing options have adapted. Here is what successful buyers are doing.

1. Get Fully Pre-Approved Before Touring

Not pre-qualified — pre-approved. There is a difference. A pre-approval means the lender has reviewed your income, assets, credit, and employment and is prepared to fund the loan. In a market where good homes under $500,000 still attract multiple offers, a pre-approval letter from a reputable local lender gives your offer immediate credibility.

2. Focus on Total Monthly Cost, Not Just Price

Your monthly payment includes principal, interest, property taxes, homeowners insurance, and possibly HOA dues and flood insurance. In Carrollwood, property taxes run approximately 1.7-2.0% of assessed value depending on whether you have homestead exemption. Insurance costs have stabilized somewhat from their 2023-2024 peaks, but they remain a meaningful budget item. Factor everything in before falling in love with a home at the top of your price range.

3. Understand What You Are Competing Against

Cash buyers still account for roughly 28-30% of Carrollwood transactions. If you are financing, you may lose some bidding wars to cash offers — especially at lower price points. Do not let this discourage you. The majority of homes still sell to financed buyers, and a strong pre-approval, flexible closing timeline, and clean offer terms can absolutely compete with cash.

4. Explore All Financing Options

Conventional loans are not the only game in town. FHA loans with 3.5% down, VA loans with zero down for eligible veterans, and various down payment assistance programs through Hillsborough County can make homeownership in Carrollwood more accessible than many buyers realize. Some builders offering new construction in the Carrollwood area are also providing rate buydown incentives that can significantly reduce your effective rate for the first few years.

5. Do Not Skip the Inspection

Many Carrollwood homes were built in the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s. That means you may encounter polybutylene plumbing, older electrical panels, aging roofs, and other issues common to homes of that vintage. A thorough inspection protects you and gives you leverage to negotiate repairs or price adjustments. It is also critical for securing homeowners insurance in today's Florida market.

For a step-by-step walkthrough of the entire buying process, the Carrollwood home buying guide covers everything from search to closing.

Carrollwood Investment Properties — Rental Demand and ROI

Carrollwood has quietly become one of the stronger rental markets in Hillsborough County, and in 2026 the fundamentals continue to support buy-and-hold investment strategies. Here is why investors are paying attention.

Rental Demand Drivers

  • Affordability gap keeps renters renting. With mortgage payments (including taxes and insurance) on a median-priced home running $2,800-$3,200 per month, many would-be buyers remain renters by necessity. This sustains demand for quality rental properties.
  • School quality attracts family renters. Families who want their children in Carrollwood-zoned schools but cannot yet purchase are willing to pay premium rents to live in the area.
  • Professional tenant base. Proximity to Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, and major hospitals creates a steady pipeline of professional renters — pilots, medical personnel, corporate transferees — who want convenient, well-maintained housing.
  • Low vacancy rates. Rental vacancy in the Carrollwood area is running approximately 4-5%, well below the national average and indicative of persistent demand.

Single-family homes remain the dominant segment, accounting for roughly 70% of all residential sales in the Carrollwood area. The median of $478,000 reflects strong activity across the $375K-$575K core range. View current Carrollwood homes for sale to see what is on the market today.

Condos are seeing the softest price growth, up just 1.8% year-over-year. This is partly due to rising HOA fees and special assessments in some older condo communities, and partly because Florida's new condo safety legislation (SB 4-D and its successors) has created additional reserve requirements that are hitting HOA budgets. Buyers shopping Carrollwood condos should carefully review association financials and reserve studies before committing.

Townhomes are the surprise performer. Limited new townhome construction in the area combined with strong demand from first-time buyers and downsizers has created a supply squeeze. Well-maintained townhomes are consistently selling within three weeks of listing.

Lakefront and waterfront properties continue to command a significant premium. Carrollwood has numerous lakes and retention ponds, and homes with direct water access or expansive water views consistently outperform the broader market in both appreciation and buyer interest. The Carrollwood waterfront homes page tracks available lakefront listings.
